transcript:
Meeting: LatticeWave / Redwood quickstart fastpass + privacy check
Date: 2028-11-21 09:30 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Nina Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Evan Park (LatticeWave CTO), Maya Singh (ML Eng), Carlos Rivera (Infra), Olivia Chen (Data Privacy), Samir Patel (Product)

Summary: Quick discovery to confirm LatticeWave's path from free credits to pilot. Main concerns: latency/cost tradeoffs, private VPC deployment timing, SOC2/audit log access, and time-to-first-token for PLG users. Redwood to send quickstart + credits and run early perf recipe.

Topics: quickstart tokens, hosted vs dedicated vs private timeline, VPC/SSO/KMS, perf expectations (latency at 50–500ms), eval prompts, security questionnaire, bench run plan

Questions: Who owns infra for pilot? What are production SLOs? Do you need on-prem or just VPC? Which stakeholders for security review?

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan here from Redwood, I'm the AE. Um, Priya our solutions engineer is on the line, and Nina from customer success. How's it going Evan?
[00:08] Evan: Hi Jordan, good morning. We're excited to, uh, see how fast we can get our product prototype using Redwood's hosted API.
[00:14] Maya: Morning. We want to understand time-to-first-token for our PLG onboarding flow — it's basically critical.
[00:20] Priya: Great, thanks. Quick clarifying question, is the goal for your PLG path to keep everything on hosted initially and only move to Dedicated or Private later?
[00:28] Samir: Yeah that's what we were thinking, hosted for initial signups, then a pilot for heavy enterprise customers maybe with Private VPC.
[00:35] Carlos: Right, and from infra side we want to know burst behavior, cold-starts, and how KV cache — K V cash — is handled across model shards.
[00:44] Jordan: Good callout. So the quickstart, the free credits we provide, should get you to first token inside hours — typically under an hour if you follow the SDK flow. We'll send the quickstart repo link and a tiny checklist.
[00:56] Evan: Under an hour sound good. Is that for streaming as well? Our onboarding uses streaming completions to show progressive results.
[01:04] Priya: Yes, streaming's supported on hosted. The only caveat is if you request ultra-low latency with high QPS you may want to consider Dedicated. For the PLG path, hosted is generally fine.
[01:14] Maya: What do you mean by "ultra-low" in numbers? We're targeting p95 latencies below 300ms for short prompts (~64 tokens).
[01:22] Priya: For 64 tokens on our optimised models you'll typically see about 80–250ms p95 on Hosted in our US regions, depending on load and batching. For consistent sub-100ms at scale, Dedicated with pinned pools is recommended.
[01:35] Carlos: Ok so sounds like hosted meets our early needs. What's the billing model during the free credits period — do you throttle beyond credits?
[01:43] Jordan: Free credits are just credits applied to your account, you'll need to set up billing to continue. We'll also show per-route token estimates in the console so you can watch costs.
[01:53] Olivia: From the privacy side, do you retain request payloads? We need retention policies since we handle moderately sensitive user messages.
[02:00] Jordan: Hosted offers configurable retention; default is 30 days but you can request shorter retention or opt into Private where logs never leave your VPC (or you can bring-your-own KMS). We'll attach the retention and data-flow doc — note that transcription may show "Redwoo" in some places haha.
[02:16] Evan: (laughs) that's fine. Regarding SOC 2, do you have report access for vendor assessments?
[02:22] Nina: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and provide a compliance pack for pilots and enterprise procurement. We'll share the SOC 2 summary and the security questionnaire.
[02:30] Olivia: Great. Also looking for SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning on the Console.
[02:35] Priya: Both supported. SAML, SCIM, RBAC — those are in our Private and Dedicated offerings too, but the hosted Console supports SSO for admin accounts.
[02:45] Samir: Do you have any customers that started hosted and then moved to Private? Curious about migration friction.
[02:51] Jordan: Yes, a few. The API layer is the same, so it's mostly configuration and networking — pinning model versions, and if you want to go air-gapped we'd run an onboarding with our Private team. Priya can share a migration checklist.
[03:04] Priya: I'll do that. Also we usually provide a perf-benchmark recipe — same model, same prompt set you give us, we run hosted and give you ranges for latency/cost and then show Dedicated estimates.
[03:15] Maya: Perfect. We'll send representative prompts. Quick question on quantization — are the models you serve quantized and does that affect determinism?
[03:24] Priya: We use quantized variants for cost efficiency on some hosts; determinism can vary a bit across quantization and kernel selection. But we track quality regressions in Redwood Optimize and flag regressions tied to your eval suite.
[03:36] Evan: Redwood Optimize, got it. We might want to run a small quality regression check in the pilot.
[03:41] Priya: Definitely — if you provide prompts and expected outputs we can run an eval and show metrics.
[03:46] Carlos: Network-wise for VPC, how does private deployment talk to the control plane? Do we need outbound rules?
[03:52] Priya: For Private VPC, control plane can be customer-managed with optional peering. There are configurations for air-gapped installs too but that takes more lead time. For the usual VPC setup you'll need specific egress to the control plane endpoints — we'll include the infra diagram.
[04:06] Olivia: Lead time on Private? We have a compliance window — can't be more than 8 weeks from contract signature ideally.
[04:13] Jordan: For a typical Private VPC onboarding 6–10 weeks is reasonable; full on-prem air-gapped is longer. If you need <8 weeks we can scope a dedicated pilot and prioritize.
[04:24] Samir: Pricing question — what does Dedicated look like compared to Hosted on a per-token basis?
[04:29] Jordan: Dedicated is a commitment-based model where unit cost drops with reserved capacity. We'll include a sample pricing sheet — for example a reserved pool might reduce per-token cost by 30–50% but you pay for reserved GPU hours.
[04:42] Evan: Ok. Also are there any rate limits on trial accounts that could affect our PLG flows?
[04:48] Jordan: Trial accounts have soft rate limits to prevent abuse; we can bump them for pilots. The Console shows per-route throttles.
[04:55] Maya: About time-to-first-token for signups, if a user signs up and we spin up a session, are there cold start latencies we should design around?
[05:03] Priya: Cold-starts are mostly about model warm-up and KV cache priming. We have prefix caching strategies and continuous background warm pools in Dedicated to reduce cold starts. On Hosted cold-starts are usually a few hundred ms for small models but can be more for larger family models.
[05:18] Carlos: Does Redwood manage KV caches across shards or is that per-instance?
[05:23] Priya: The runtime manages KV cache; it's per-serving process but with cache-sharing optimisations across warm workers. The transcribed notes might read cache as "kay vee cash" sometimes.
[05:33] (laughter)
[05:36] Jordan: Onbench plan — Priya will run a hosted run with your sample prompts, we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token costs. Then if you want, we can simulate a Dedicated estimate.
[05:46] Evan: Sounds good. For the bench run what inputs do you need?
[05:50] Priya: A CSV of prompts, expected output lengths, target QPS, and target p95 SLO. If you add any edge-case prompts that break things, include them.
[05:59] Maya: We'll prepare that by Friday.
[06:02] Jordan: Cool. Any blockers on security?
[06:05] Olivia: We'll need the SOC 2, encryption-at-rest details, KMS integration for Private, and access to audit logs for the pilot. Also, do you support customer-managed KMS keys in hosted?
[06:16] Nina: In hosted we support bring-your-own-key for certain plans; for Private you can fully manage keys. We'll include a KMS matrix.
[06:24] Carlos: For logging, we need to export audit logs to our SIEM. Can we stream logs?
[06:29] Priya: Yes, audit log export is supported — we can push to S3 or to a logging endpoint. We'll attach the logging integration doc.
[06:37] Samir: Any gotchas if we run long-running prompts? We have some streaming summarization jobs that may exceed 1k tokens.
[06:45] Priya: Large token counts increase latency and cost; we have chunking and streaming helpers. For very long sessions we recommend batching or using a reranker pattern to keep cost down.
[06:55] Jordan: Let's talk timeline and decision criteria. Evan?
[06:58] Evan: We're aiming to get a working prototype in two weeks, a pilot with a handful of enterprise customers in 6–8 weeks, and decide on Dedicated vs Private after pilot. Success criteria: p95 below 350ms for main flows, cost per session under $0.10, and security sign-off.
[07:17] Jordan: Great, that aligns well. We'll target the 2-week prototype using free credits and quickstart.
[07:22] Maya: For the prototype can we get 10k free tokens? That should be enough for smoke tests.
[07:27] Jordan: Yep, we'll issue a 10k token credit to your account and include a usage tracker.
[07:32] Evan: Awesome. Pricing for longer-term usage — is there a minimum for Dedicated?
[07:36] Jordan: Dedicated typically has monthly minimums tied to GPU reservations — we'll include sample tiers.
[07:42] Olivia: One more compliance question — will we get per-request metadata for audit (user id, request id)?
[07:48] Priya: Yes, request metadata can be included and forwarded to logs. We'll document the schema.
[07:54] Carlos: When you run the perf bench, do you simulate multi-tenant noise? Our PLG stack could have many small tenants interleaving requests.
[08:02] Priya: We can run multi-tenant style loads in the bench; please indicate typical concurrency distribution.
[08:08] Jordan: Quick note — we'll also share a short sample app that wires the SDK to a signup button so you can see true time-to-first-token from signup to UI display.
[08:17] Samir: That would help product folks a lot.
[08:20] Maya: We'll need a short sandbox session with Priya to step through authentication and the streaming example.
[08:25] Priya: I'll set that up for the week of 11/27. Preferences on timezone?
[08:30] Maya: Morning PST works.
[08:32] Jordan: Great. Any other blockers or competitors you are evaluating?
[08:36] Evan: We're also looking at Anthropic's API and OpenAI — mostly comparing per-token unit economics and privacy controls.
[08:42] Jordan: Helpful to know. We'll try to include a short comparison doc — cost and privacy tradeoffs.
[08:48] Olivia: Please include audit scope and retention options in that pack.
[08:51] Priya: Will do.
[08:53] (brief pause)
[09:00] Jordan: Ok I'll summarize next steps — send quickstart + 10k credits, share SOC 2 and security pack, Priya to run perf bench and schedule sandbox, customer to send prompt set and SLOs. Any questions?
[09:11] Evan: No, that's clear. Thanks everyone.
[09:14] Maya: Thanks.
[09:15] Olivia: Thanks.
[09:16] Jordan: Great, we'll follow up by Friday.
[09:20] End of call.

Recap and next steps (verbatim):
- Jordan: Issue 10k token credit, send quickstart repo and onboarding checklist (due 2028-11-24).
- Priya: Run a hosted perf run using customer's prompt CSV and share latency/cost numbers (due 2028-11-28).
- Maya: Provide representative prompt set and target SLOs (due 2028-11-25).
- Olivia: Confirm security questionnaire contacts and required docs (due 2028-11-26).

Linked artifacts mentioned: quickstart repo (link to be shared), SOC 2 summary (attachment), perf-benchmark recipe (attachment), data-retention-and-kms-matrix (attachment)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., KV cache as "kay vee cash", Redwood as "Redwoo"), speaker overlap at times.
